source_text: Ταῦτα δέ, ἀγαπητοί μου, οὐκ ἐπεὶ ἔγνων τινὰς ἐξ ὑμῶν οὕτως ἔχοντας, ἀλλ’ ὡς μικρότερος ὑμῶν θέλω προφυλάσσεσθαι ὑμᾶς, μὴ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς τὰ ἄγκιστρα τῆς κενοδοξίας, ἀλλὰ πεπληροφορῆσθαι ἐν τῇ γεννήσει καὶ τῷ πάθει καὶ τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ γενομένῃ ἐν καιρῷ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Ποντίου Πιλάτου: πραχθέντα ἀληθῶς καὶ βεβαίως ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν, ἧς ἐκτραπῆναι μηδενὶ ὑμῶν γένοιτο.
thought_title: Why Ignatius warns against empty glory
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, explaining that his warning about Judaism and false teaching is not because he knows them to be at fault, but because he wants to protect them.
pass_a_gloss: But these things, my beloved ones, I say not because I knew some of you to be so disposed, but as one smaller than you I want you to be guarded beforehand, not to fall into the hooks of empty glory, but to be fully assured in the birth and the passion and the resurrection that happened in the time of the governorship of Pontius Pilate: these things were done truly and certainly by Jesus Christ, our hope, from which may it not happen to any of you to be turned aside.

choices.why: The compound means 'empty opinion/glory' and is the source of the vice Ignatius warns against; 'vainglory' is the traditional rendering but 'empty glory' keeps the literal force of κενός + δόξα.
The perfect passive infinitive conveys a settled state of complete conviction; 'fully assured' captures the perfective force.
γέννησις refers to the act of being born, Christ's incarnation; 'birth' is the literal and precise rendering.
ἡγεμονία is the office or period of a Roman governor; 'governorship' is the standard literal rendering for the administrative term.

choices.english: from which may it not happen to any of you to be turned aside
choices.why: The optative γένοιτο with μηδενί expresses a wish that no one be turned aside from the hope; the passive infinitive ἐκτραπῆναι keeps the subject as 'any of you'.
rejected: from which may none of you be turned aside
which may it not befall any of you to abandon

pass_b_english: Now, my beloved, I am not writing these things because I have learned that any of you are actually in this condition. I write because, as one who is less than you, I want to guard you beforehand, so that you do not fall into the hooks of empty glory. Be fully assured instead in the birth, the passion, and the resurrection that took place in the time of the governorship of Pontius Pilate. These things were truly and certainly accomplished by Jesus Christ, our hope. May none of you ever be turned aside from Him.

last_rejected.why: Not a glossary term; no issue.
last_rejected.ruling: ἡγεμονίας correctly rendered as 'governorship'; no glossary issue exists here.

last_rejected.quote: may it not happen to any of you to be turned aside
last_rejected.why: The relative pronoun ἧς (feminine, referring to ἐλπίδος/hope) means 'from which' [hope], not 'from which' [these things]. The English 'from which' grammatically could refer to 'Jesus Christ, our hope' but is awkwardly placed after 'accomplished by Jesus Christ, our hope'. The Greek says 'from which [hope] may it not happen to any of you to be turned aside.' The English 'from which' appears to modify the preceding clause's events rather than hope itself, slightly obscuring that turning aside is from THE HOPE specifically.
last_rejected.fix: our hope, from which may none of you be turned aside.
last_rejected.ruling: ἧς 'from which' correctly renders the relative; antecedent ἐλπίδος is clear enough in English context.

problems.why: 'Governorship' is technically correct (prefect/procurator) but may seem like anachronistic modern title.

fixed: Changed 'governorship' to 'prefecture' to better reflect the Roman title (ἡγεμονίας) without anachronism.

problems.quote: the birth, the passion, and the resurrection that took place during the time when Pontius Pilate governed
problems.why: Birth under Pilate? Chronology wrong; birth under Herod, passion under Pilate.
problems.fix: Check: Ignatius may mean 'incarnation' or 'appearing' broadly.

edits.old: the birth, the passion, and the resurrection that took place during the time when Pontius Pilate governed
edits.new: the birth, the passion, and the resurrection that took place in the time of the governorship of Pontius Pilate

fixed: The source reads 'ἐν τῇ γεννήσει καὶ τῷ πάθει καὶ τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ γενομένῃ ἐν καιρῷ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Ποντίου Πιλάτου' — 'in the birth and the passion and the resurrection that happened in the time of the governorship of Pontius Pilate.' The English 'during the time when Pontius Pilate governed' is a faithful rendering of 'ἐν καιρῷ τῆς ἡγεμονίας Ποντίου Πιλάτου.' The reported problem about birth under Herod is a theological/historical concern, not a mistranslation of the Greek. The source itself places all three events in the time of Pilate's governorship, so the English correctly reflects the source. No edit needed for meaning; however, I restored the earlier edit's 'governorship' phrasing to match the source's 'ἡγεμονίας' more closely, as the earlier edit had been reverted.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker's purpose, broke long sentences into natural modern units, made the implied object 'Him' explicit in the final clause, and replaced the technical term 'prefecture' with a clearer phrase while preserving every claim.

notes.why: 'Governorship' is technically correct (prefect/procurator) but may seem like anachronistic modern title.
